title: Cache and log leakage
summary: Caches and logs hold copies of permissioned content outside the ACL. A semantic cache can answer one user from another user's retrieved documents, and a content log can expose what the index protected.
useIf: You cache answers, embeddings or prompts, or you log prompts, chunks or responses.
avoidIf: You have no cache and log identifiers only. Then this topic is already satisfied.

explain.md: The index enforces ACLs. Everything downstream that stores content does not. Four stores matter: **provider prompt caches**, your **exact-match response cache**, a **semantic cache** and **logs and stored conversation state**.

explain.caption: Where permissioned content can leak (checked 2026-10-13)
head: Store
Leak vector
Scoping control
rows: Provider prompt cache
Reuse of an identical prefix across users

OpenAI: not shared across organizations, with an optional prompt_cache_key [[tr10]]. Azure OpenAI: not shared across subscriptions [[r30]]. Anthropic: per organization, and per workspace on several surfaces [[tr11]]
Semantic cache
A similar question returns an answer built from another user's documents
Azure API Management llm-semantic-cache-lookup with vary-by on user or group id, and a strict score-threshold [[r28]]
Exact-match response cache
Same question, different rights
Key on the normalized question plus the caller's ACL scope
Logs and stored state
Content copied into a store with no ACLs
Log ids and decisions. Responses API, threads and stored completions keep history at rest in your Foundry resource, so they need retention and access rules [[r38]]

explain.md: **Semantic caches** need the most care. The APIM policy uses a `score-threshold` from 0.0 to 1.0 where lower means a stricter match. The docs suggest starting near 0.05 and warn that values above 0.2 may cause mismatches, and that semantic caching can return incorrect, outdated or unsafe answers. `vary-by` partitions the cache, for example by user or group id, to control cross-user access [[r28]].

**Provider prompt caches** are scoped by the provider, and same-tenant users share an entry only when the whole prefix matches, which already includes the same retrieved text (design reasoning). Use `prompt_cache_key` for accounting or routing, not as a security control [[tr10]]. A timing side-channel audit (ICML 2025) found global cache sharing across users in seven API providers at study time and showed timing differences can leak other users' prompts. Provider docs now state organization or workspace scoping, so read the paper as the reason to prefer scoped caches and not as current behaviour [[r29]].

explain.title: A cache TTL is part of the revocation SLA
explain.md: A cached answer outlives a revoked grant by up to its TTL. Set the TTL below the revocation target, and skip the cache when any source document carries a restricted label (design reasoning).

whereToUse: Cost reduction work that adds a semantic or response cache in front of generation
Logging design for assistants over permissioned content
Reviews of stateful features such as stored conversations or threads
Multi-user gateways where one cache serves different principals

use: Scope every cache entry by ACL scope or user
Keep TTLs below the revocation target
Log ids and decisions by default
avoid: A global semantic cache over permissioned answers
Loosening the similarity threshold to raise hit rate
Writing full prompts and chunks to a broadly readable log workspace
flips: ACL scope is nearly unique per user: a semantic cache has a near-zero hit rate, so drop it
Content is public: a shared cache is fine
An incident needs content: capture it for a bounded window under its own access control

pitfalls.symptom: A user gets an answer citing documents they cannot open
pitfalls.cause: A semantic cache served another user's answer
pitfalls.fix: Partition with vary-by on the ACL scope and tighten the threshold

pitfalls.symptom: A revoked user still gets the old answer
pitfalls.cause: The answer cache TTL is longer than the revocation target
pitfalls.fix: Shorten the TTL and key by ACL scope

pitfalls.symptom: Support staff can read confidential prompts
pitfalls.cause: The log workspace has broad read and holds full content
pitfalls.fix: Log ids and decisions, and put any content capture under its own access control and expiry

pitfalls.cause: Stored state in the Responses API or threads was not covered by retention rules
pitfalls.fix: Include stateful stores in deletion and access reviews [[r38]]

scenarios.title: Semantic cache for 5,000 employees
scenarios.situation: An internal assistant sees many repeated questions. Cost is high. Groups define access, and employees fall into a few hundred distinct group sets. Revocation target is one hour.
unknowns: Do restricted labels exist in the corpus?
How similar are repeated questions in a scope?
scenarios.question: How do you cache?

options.name: A global semantic cache with a loose threshold for hit rate
options.why: It will return answers built from other users' documents and above 0.2 it may mismatch [[r28]].

options.name: Exact-match cache keyed by user
options.tradeoff: Low hit rate because each user is a separate key.

options.name: Semantic cache partitioned by ACL scope with vary-by, a strict threshold, a TTL under an hour and a skip for restricted labels
options.why: Users in the same scope share answers, and the TTL fits the revocation target.
options.tradeoff: More cache entries, tuning, and a bypass rule to maintain.

flips.if: Scope is nearly unique per user
flips.then: The semantic cache rarely hits, so drop it.
Shorten the TTL or remove the cache for restricted tiers.

scenarios.takeaway: Partition semantic caches by ACL scope.

scenarios.title: Debugging needs versus content in logs
scenarios.situation: Engineers want full prompts and retrieved chunks in logs to debug bad answers. The log workspace is readable by a large operations group. Documents are confidential.
unknowns: Can access to the log store be narrowed?
scenarios.question: What do you log?

options.name: Document ids, principal id, filter hash and decision by default, with content capture only for a bounded window under its own access control
options.why: Ids reproduce the retrieval, and content is available only when an incident needs it.
options.tradeoff: Debugging text quality takes an extra step.

options.name: Full prompts and chunks to the shared workspace
options.why: It copies ACL-protected text into a store with broad read access.
options.tradeoff: Acceptable for public content in a private workspace.

options.name: Redacted snippets only
options.tradeoff: Redaction misses things and the store still needs access control.

flips.then: Open a time-limited capture with its own ACL and delete after.

scenarios.takeaway: Logs copy content out of the ACL, so default to ids.

scenarios.title: prompt_cache_key as a tenant wall
scenarios.situation: A team plans to set prompt_cache_key per tenant and says that stops tenants sharing cached prefixes, so they can put any tenant's documents in a shared prefix.
unknowns: What does the provider say about cache scope?
What is actually in the shared prefix?
scenarios.question: How do you respond?

options.name: Treat the key as routing and accounting, rely on provider scoping, and keep tenant documents out of any shared prefix
options.why: Caches are not shared across organizations, and the key is not documented as a security control [[tr10]].

options.name: Use the key as the isolation control and put tenant data in the shared prefix
options.why: It turns a hit-rate setting into a security claim it does not make.
options.tradeoff: Fine to use as accounting alongside enforced separation.

options.name: Disable prompt caching everywhere
options.tradeoff: Higher cost and latency for stable prefixes.

flips.then: Share them freely and keep tenant content in the suffix.
The default becomes in-memory retention for models that support both modes, so check the retention setting per model [[tr10]].

scenarios.takeaway: Cache keys tune hit rate. They do not enforce access.

quiz.q: Users report seeing answers that cite documents they cannot open. A semantic cache sits in front of generation. What is the most likely fix?
options: Partition the cache with vary-by on the ACL scope and tighten the similarity threshold
Switch to a larger embedding model
quiz.explain: The cache returned another user's answer. Partitioning by ACL scope and tightening the threshold prevents cross-user hits. A longer TTL makes it worse, and temperature or model size are unrelated.

quiz.q: Which statements are supported by provider documentation? Choose all that apply.
options: OpenAI prompt caches are not shared across organizations
Azure OpenAI prompt caches are not shared between Azure subscriptions
prompt_cache_key is a security control for tenant isolation
Anthropic isolates caches per workspace on the Claude API
quiz.explain: OpenAI, Azure OpenAI and Anthropic documents state organization, subscription and workspace scoping. prompt_cache_key routes and separates accounting and is not described as a security control.

flashcards.front: What do APIM's score-threshold and vary-by do for semantic caches?
flashcards.back: score-threshold sets match strictness (lower is stricter, start near 0.05, above 0.2 may mismatch). vary-by partitions the cache, for example by user or group id.
No. It routes requests and separates cache accounting. Isolation comes from provider scoping by organization, subscription or workspace and from your own design.

flashcards.front: What should logs hold by default for permissioned content?
flashcards.back: Document ids, principal id, filter hash and the decision. Capture content only for a bounded window under its own access control.
